A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MemSinks work. Their complete main text, Figures 1–7, Tables 1–6, equations, and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original TinyStories memorization and localization experiments, robustness analyses, and larger-scale SmolLM pretraining results in Figures 2–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes, including the TinyStories and larger-scale SmolLM results.

M1.justification: The shared/sink neuron partition, deterministic sequence-dependent masking, training procedure, and removal of sink neurons during evaluation remain unchanged (Section 5; Appendices G and I).

E1.justification: Both versions use TS-Repetition, TS-Canary, and the SlimPajama/TinyStories pretraining mixture. No dataset, task, domain, or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain pruning/Hard-Concrete, integrated gradients, gradient masking, and standard training with and without repeated data. Comparator membership in Figures 2–6 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Data construction, loss-based metrics, model configurations, and training settings match. Examples include 100 stories repeated 128 times and the 1-billion/2-billion-token larger-scale runs; Tables 1–6 retain identical hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The activation-ratio and model-size analyses, sequence-ID noise tests, and single-sequence learning/forgetting study are retained without revision (Sections 5.3–5.4; Figures 5 and 7).

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies experimental repeat counts, run-to-run uncertainty estimates, or significance tests, and the figures retain the same reporting.

E6.justification: The plotted results in Figures 2–7 are identical, and numerical findings in the text match, including the roughly 66% comparison in Section 5.1 and at-least-50% loss-gap reduction in Section 5.2. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 and the definitions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs in Appendices D, F, and H are unchanged. Mathematical differences are confined to typesetting and reflow.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about mechanistic entanglement, isolating memorization through MemSinks, and preserving generalization in the demonstrated settings.

C2.justification: The forgetting and co-adaptation explanations are retained. Section 6 preserves the limitations concerning controlled experiments, sequence metadata, broader capability testing, and untested adversarial extraction.

D1.justification: v2 adds an AR-FORUM/MemSinks repository address and a project website on its title page. The older grghosal/MemSinks address remains in the abstract and Appendix I. Implementation details and hyperparameters are unchanged; the PDFs do not establish changes to the linked resources themselves.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A, and the cited works retain the same research positioning. Expanded bibliographic author names and citation-style changes do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: Author/affiliation and header text, citation conventions, and bibliographic formatting change. The section sequence, substantive paragraphs, terminology, and narrative remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from two columns to one, with a redesigned title page, changed typography and caption styling, and extensive figure/table relocation. The same seven figures and six tables remain. Bibliographic URL overlaps visible in v1 are resolved.

improvement.justification: v2 provides modest readability and navigation gains: the bibliography resolves long-URL collisions visible on v1 PDF page 11, and the title page makes repository and project links easier to find. The methods, experimental evidence, proofs, and limitations remain unchanged, limiting the overall improvement to presentation and access information.
